source: CARDI (2011), "Handbook of Integrated Techniques for Increasing Wet-Season and Dry-Season Rice Productivity" (Khmer, 50pp, funded by CAVAC/ACIAR, foreword by H.E. Chan Sarun, Minister of Agriculture, dated 26 August 2011)
text: Broadcasting (sowing seed directly into the puddled field rather than raising and transplanting seedlings) saves labor and time over transplanting, but it demands a well-leveled field, a higher seeding rate, and more diligent, regular weeding, since there are no row gaps to walk and weed between as there are with transplanting. On-farm comparisons found no meaningful yield difference between a broadcast crop and a transplanted crop of the same variety when both receive the same standard of care (fertilizing, weeding and water management) — the choice of method does not by itself determine yield. Farmers who broadcast using traditional varieties they save themselves from season to season (rather than buying certified seed) are specifically advised to maintain the small seed-purification nursery plot described separately, since broadcasting with unpurified, self-saved seed compounds the yield and quality losses that come from varietal impurity.
